title: A smaller gain after IBM's cash adjustments
question: Why was the nine-month gain in IBM-defined free cash flow smaller than the operating-cash gain?
comparability_limits: Use the directly reported nine-month columns together in Q3 table 8. Do not sum the three quarterly cash tables or substitute Q3-only cash.

GAAP operating cash and IBM-defined non-GAAP free cash flow are separate measures. IBM removes the change in Financing receivables, then adds signed net capital expenditures. Free cash flow is not merely consolidated OCF less capex.
DIFFERENCE inputs are current then prior. Financing delta is (2,805 - 905) times -1; capex delta is -1,200 minus -1,067, with no second negation. Gain in reported FCF is 7,787 minus 7,181.

2026 rounded levels yield 11,791 - 2,805 - 1,200 = 7,786, versus reported 7,787. Prior levels reconcile exactly to 7,181. The resulting change bridge yields 605 versus reported 606. These are the same one-million cash rounding issue, separate from revenue's two-million differences.
The financing adjustment is an accounting-definition reconciliation. Its increase alone proves neither deteriorating credit, manipulated earnings nor weak Software demand.

Consolidated cash does not establish Software-specific cash generation, deferred-business conversion, distributable shareholder cash or a full cash-balance bridge. Acquisitions, debt and dividends are outside this FCF comparison.

Consolidated IBM cash; not Software cash conversion or a full cash-balance bridge.
